code.originalText: Eight-day review with the reticulocyte response and potassium, seen the same day by hematology: the cause, the injection plan, endoscopy, autoimmune screening and the nerves

text.paragraph: Eight-day review with the reticulocyte response, seen the same day by hematology. [S]

Admiral Peary returns eight days after starting cyanocobalamin and is seen by Dr. Abernethy-Kwan of hematology on the same day. He has had five of the seven loading injections, given by the clinic nurse every other day. His tongue is less sore and he has a little more energy, though he is still breathless on the stairs. The numbness and pins and needles in his feet are unchanged; he has had no falls, and he checks his feet each morning. He has had no palpitations, muscle cramps or weakness. His potassium, planned with the second injection, was not drawn then. Blood for intrinsic factor and parietal cell antibodies, gastrin and thyroid antibodies was drawn this morning before his fifth injection. [S]

list.item:
Pernicious anemia (D51.0). Dr. Abernethy-Kwan confirms pernicious anemia: severe vitamin B12 deficiency with a high methylmalonic acid, a positive intrinsic factor antibody, which is highly specific, a positive parietal cell antibody and a high gastrin from loss of acid-producing cells. The reticulocyte peak of 7.9% at day 8 confirms the response. No transfusion is needed: he is stable at rest and his count is rising. [S]
Finish the seven loading doses, then cyanocobalamin 1,000 micrograms weekly, self-injected, until the nerves stop improving, then monthly for life.
Upper endoscopy with biopsies, with a screening colonoscopy at the same session.
Standing order for potassium with any future loading course.

Subacute combined degeneration (G32.0). Posterior column and peripheral nerve signs unchanged after one week, as expected; recovery takes months and may be incomplete. [S]
Physical therapy for balance and gait.
Neurological examination at each visit.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: Guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of cobalamin and folate disorders (2014); Vitamin B12 deficiency in over 16s: diagnosis and management (NG239) (2024); AGA Clinical Practice Update on the Diagnosis and Management of Atrophic Gastritis: Expert Review (2021); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, anemia and depression, bipolar, and mood disorders monographs (2026); Guidelines on the prevention of foot ulcers in persons with diabetes (IWGDF 2023 update) (2023); Falls Prevention in Community-Dwelling Older Adults: Interventions (2024)

Follow-up: Last two loading doses with the nurse, then weekly self-injection. Five-week review on the day of the endoscopy and colonoscopy. Call for palpitations, cramps, weakness, a fall, or any wound on the feet. Next scheduled visit 1919-02-17: five-week review on the day of upper endoscopy and colonoscopy: blood count, nerves, falls and feet. [S]
